synopsis: Scenic is an open-source, free probabilistic scenario language with native 3D geometry, lane-independent object placement, and interfaces to Python and multiple simulators [f6693, f16024, f9211, f9212]. The booklet considers its programmable semantics adaptable to job sites and better suited to pits, stockpiles and loading areas than road-oriented languages, but Scenic is not a standard and no mining or construction deployment or off-road evidence was found [f8636, f6694, f8637, f9209]. It recommends Scenic or an in-house YAML schema with an OpenODD-style taxonomy for a manufacturer-owned, domain-neutral, version-controlled scenario catalog, with OpenSCENARIO export where required [f14491, f7198]. Scenic integrates with VerifAI for falsification; on-road work in 2021 reported up to a fivefold speed-up from parallel multi-objective falsification, without establishing off-road performance [f16025, f6839, f9209]. Scenic appears in the lowest-cost example tool chain, but its enterprise test governance is thinner than commercial tools', a trustworthy 2026 release date was not found, and funding, maintenance and security-patch cadence were not examined [f9266, f8638, f9213, f9392, f9393].
